summary: Crop with the `crop` video filter: `-vf crop=w:h:x:y`. Width and height come first, then the top-left corner of the kept region, all in pixels of the SOURCE frame. Omit x and y and the crop is centred. Cropping re-encodes, so `-c copy` cannot be combined with `-vf`; pick an encoder and a quality target explicitly or ffmpeg picks defaults you did not choose. Encoders that need even dimensions (libx264 with yuv420p) fail on an odd width or height, which is why `crop=iw-2*20:ih` style expressions are preferred over literal odd numbers.

examples.title: Crop a centred 1280x720 window
examples.code: ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf crop=1280:720 -c:v libx264 -crf 20 -c:a copy out.mp4

examples.title: Trim 20px off every edge, staying even-dimensioned
examples.code: ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf crop=iw-2*20:ih-2*20 -c:v libx264 -crf 20 -c:a copy out.mp4
